subject: Business
title: Confirmation Bias: Seeing What You Expect
description: A quick win: understand Confirmation Bias: Seeing What You Expect.

hook.text: You think your product is great. So you read every positive review and skip the negative ones.

buildup.text: Confirmation bias means we seek evidence that supports what we already believe.

discovery.text: Peter Wason's card experiment showed people test rules by looking for confirming cases, not disconfirming ones.

twist.text: Scientists are supposed to be objective. Studies show they interpret ambiguous data to match their hypothesis.

climax.text: The antidote: actively seek reasons you might be wrong. Ask 'What would change my mind?'

punchline.text: We don't see the world as it is. We see it as we are.

quiz.question: What is confirmation bias?
options: Seeking evidence that supports existing beliefs
Being overly confident in your abilities

details.summary: Confirmation bias drives people to seek, interpret, and remember information that confirms their existing beliefs while ignoring contradictory evidence. In business, it causes leaders to double down on failing strategies and analysts to cherry-pick supporting data.
details.whyItMatters: Confirmation bias is among the most pervasive and damaging cognitive biases in business. It undermines market research, strategic planning, and hiring decisions by creating false confidence in flawed conclusions.
takeaways: People actively seek information confirming their existing beliefs
Contradictory evidence is dismissed, reinterpreted, or simply not noticed
Devil's advocate roles and pre-mortems help counter confirmation bias

faq.question: How does confirmation bias affect business strategy?
faq.answer: Leaders who championed a strategy selectively notice data supporting it while dismissing warning signs. Market research samples are unconsciously designed to confirm hypotheses. Competitor analysis focuses on weaknesses rather than threats. These patterns delay needed pivots.

faq.question: What practical techniques reduce confirmation bias in teams?
faq.answer: Assign devil's advocate roles that rotate among team members. Run pre-mortems imagining the strategy failed. Require red team analysis for major decisions. Use structured decision frameworks that force consideration of disconfirming evidence before conclusions.
